source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 5 (Wetlands, Ramsar Sites and Marine Ecology).

sections.heading: 1. Wetlands
points: **Wetlands** = areas where water covers the soil or is present at/near the surface (marshes, mangroves, lakes, floodplains, estuaries).
Functions ('kidneys of the landscape'): **water purification, flood control, groundwater recharge, biodiversity support, carbon storage**.
Threats: drainage, pollution, encroachment, invasive species.

sections.heading: 2. Ramsar Convention
points: The **Ramsar Convention (1971, Ramsar, Iran)** — an intergovernmental treaty for the **conservation and wise use of wetlands**; came into force 1975.
Wetlands of international importance are designated **Ramsar Sites**.
India has **80+ Ramsar sites** (among the highest in Asia); examples: **Chilika Lake (Odisha), Keoladeo (Bharatpur), Loktak (Manipur), Wular (J&K), Sundarbans, Sambhar (Rajasthan)**.
The **Montreux Record** lists Ramsar sites under threat (India: Keoladeo, Loktak).

sections.heading: 3. Mangroves and Coral Reefs
points: **Mangroves** — salt-tolerant coastal forests; protect coasts from erosion/storms/tsunamis, nurseries for fish; **Sundarbans** = largest mangrove forest.
**Coral reefs** — built by tiny **coral polyps** (with symbiotic **zooxanthellae** algae); 'rainforests of the sea' — very high biodiversity.
**Coral bleaching** — corals expel their algae (due to warming/stress) and turn white; a sign of ocean stress/climate change.
Indian reefs: **Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar**.

sections.heading: 4. Marine Ecology
points: Marine ecosystems: **estuaries, coral reefs, mangroves, open ocean, deep sea**.
**Estuaries** (river meets sea) are highly productive.
Threats: overfishing, plastic/oil pollution, ocean acidification, warming.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Wetlands = 'kidneys of the landscape'; Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran).
Ramsar sites = wetlands of international importance; India has 80+.
Montreux Record = threatened Ramsar sites (India: Keoladeo, Loktak).
Coral reefs built by polyps + zooxanthellae; coral bleaching = loss of algae (warming).
Sundarbans = largest mangrove; reefs = Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, Andaman.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Ramsar Convention (1971)** is about **wetlands** (signed at Ramsar, Iran).
The **Montreux Record** lists **threatened** Ramsar wetlands.
**Coral bleaching** = corals lose their symbiotic **zooxanthellae** (due to warming).
**Sundarbans** is the **largest mangrove** forest in the world.
